speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether there will be further assistance for the self-employed beyond the Self-employed Income Relief Scheme (SIRS).

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Self-employed Person Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) is a means-tested scheme to help Singaporean self-employed persons or SEPs with less means and family support to tide over this period of economic uncertainty.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The income eligibility criteria for SIRS covered over 80% of Singaporeans with taxable income.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The annual value (AV) of the housing criteria covered about nine in 10 owner-occupied residential public and private properties.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As a proxy for family support, the spouse's income is also considered.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is a significant expansion of an already sizeable programme.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have been exercising flexibility in the qualifying criteria to support more SEPs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As SIRS was intended to support SEPs, persons who were previously unemployed or had regular employment, were redirected to the COVID-19 Support Grant.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Where there were other areas of need, we have referred unsuccessful applicants to the appropriate agencies for follow-up assistance.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Well, I would like to add, before Mr Dennis Tan begins, given the level of enthusiasm, I would like supplementary questions or SQs to just go direct to the questions and cut out the preamble.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Do not load on your SQs with tonnes of clarifications, please, so that more Members can ask questions.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: With the expanded COVID-19 Support Grant, there are some feedback that SIRS could be extended, at least at a lower payout level.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Many self-employed still have income issues in meeting their financial obligations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Large number of them were in the taxi driving profession, some in private hire car driving, a good number of them are hawkers – people whom we are very familiar with in our work as Members of Parliament.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, the performance of these sectors, of course, vary.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will have to take these factors into consideration when we look at what to do next.
